meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (national-level registration; no sub-state commercial registry)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (civil-law procedural framework incorporating U.S.-style general corporation and commercial statutes)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (investment chapter, in force 2012)
Panama–United Kingdom Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force)
Panama–Canada Free Trade Agreement with investment chapter (in force)
Panama–Mexico Free Trade Agreement with investment chapter
Panama–Singapore Free Trade Agreement with investor-state protections
Comprehensive double taxation agreements including the Netherlands, Qatar, UAE, Luxembourg, and the United Kingdom

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary instruments: Ley 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (AML/CFT framework aligned with FATF Recommendations), as amended by Ley 70 de 2019; Ley 52 de 27 de octubre de 2016 (Beneficial Ownership Register); Decreto Ejecutivo No. 54 de 17 de mayo de 2017 and complementary UAF resolutions in force (governing KYC, PEP, and UBO reporting); Ley 32 de 1927 (Sociedad Anónima formation law); Registro Público de Panamá implementing regulations for corporate and UBO registration.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every principal, beneficial owner holding 25% or more, director, and authorized signatory against OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, UK/EU sanctions lists, and Panama's national PEP lists maintained by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero. Foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, and international-organization PEPs require enhanced due diligence, documented source-of-wealth, source-of-funds verification, and senior compliance officer approval before any incorporation services are rendered. Adverse media checks and negative news assessments are mandatory under Law 23 of 2015 and applicable UAF resolutions; any positive hit triggers escalation, possible rejection of client, and, where required, filing of an Unusual Transaction Report (UTR).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá — Portal de Servicios en Línea (www.registro.gob.pa) for corporate name search, reservation, and issuance of the certificate of no opposition (Certificado de No Opusición).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names may be registered in Spanish or in Latin-script foreign languages. The legal suffix must be 'Sociedad Anónima' or 'S.A.' The chosen name must not be identical, phonetically identical, or confusingly similar to an existing registered name. Non-Latin-script names must be transliterated into Latin characters and accompanied by a certified Spanish translation before the registry search is accepted.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Panamá (when used in a manner suggesting state authority or official sponsorship)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservations are non-extendable; after expiry, a new search, fee, and reservation petition must be filed. If the Registro Público rejects a requested name, the applicant may file a corrected written petition with the Departamento de Sociedades Mercantiles within 10 working days. If the registry confirms the rejection, an administrative appeal (recurso de apelación) may be lodged with the Directora General del Registro Público within 5 business days of notification, under Law 38 of 2001. A final judicial remedy is available by filing a demanda contencioso-administrativa before the Sala Tercera of the Corte Suprema de Justicia.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted for a licensing-exempt, low-risk market-research SaaS platform, provided the virtual office consists of a physical address in Panama that is staffed and capable of receiving legal process, and provided the company designates a licensed resident agent (abogado residente). The beneficial ownership register and corporate books must be kept available for inspection by the authorities at that address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — estimated annual probability under 5% for a standard non-regulated S.A. in this exact ISIC class. The risk rises to approximately 15% if the company opens Bank/PayPal/Wise payment flows with flagged jurisdictions or if the UAF receives an unusual transaction report; otherwise, physical on-site inspection by Panamanian authorities is uncommon for license-free SaaS market research platforms.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 32 de 1927 (Panama General Corporation Law), as amended, provisions governing incorporation, capital, registered agents, and corporate governance of the Sociedad Anónima; related implementing regulations of the Registro Público de Panamá and the Tax Code for RUC registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección del Registro Mercantil
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública (public deed) containing the Pacto Social y Estatutos, recorded in the Mercantile Section as the corporate registration certificate (Ficha Registral)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. The articles may authorize capital of US$10,000 or another designated amount divided into shares, but none must be paid in at formation. Panama law does not require escrow deposit or bank verification of paid-in capital for the incorporation of a Sociedad Anónima.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board of Directors of [Company], S.A. (the 'Corporation') adopts this first written resolution. RESOLVED: 1. The subscription of the initial shares of the Corporation, as set forth in the registered articles of incorporation, is approved and accepted, and such shares are allotted to the subscribers listed on the share register. 2. The registered office at [address], Panama City, and the appointment of [Agent], S.A. as registered agent, are approved. 3. The following persons are appointed officers: [Name] as President, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Treasurer, with full powers under law. 4. The President and Secretary are authorized to execute certificates, bank forms, and regulatory filings to formalize the Corporation's existence and operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – On-line Reserva de Nombre / Mercantile Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the proposed corporate name, which must include 'S.A.' or 'Sociedad Anónima', through the Public Registry's name-reservation desk or certified online platform. Provide the incorporator's identity documents or a notarized power of attorney if acting through a registered agent. Obtain the name-reservation certificate before proceeding to notarization.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and up to two alternate names
Passport or national identity document of each incorporator
Notarized power of attorney of the registered agent, if applicable
Payment receipt for name-reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name conflicts with an existing registered entity, the Registry rejects it; submit another reservation or petition reconsideration before the Registro Público within the applicable term.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Execution of the Public Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública of the Republic of Panama; afterwards filed with the Registro Público de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the draft Pacto Social y Estatutos to a Notary Public of Panama. The incorporators or their attorney-in-fact must appear before the notary, confirm the corporate object, capital structure, share classes, registered office, and bylaw provisions, and execute the Escritura Pública. Obtain the original and certified copies for registry submission.
required_dossiers: Name-reservation certificate
Draft articles of incorporation with capital structure
Identity documents and tax identification of incorporators
Consent of the registered agent accepting appointment
Payment receipt for notarial fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects in the draft or capacity documents, amend the deed and re-execute; if the notary refuses to act, engage another licensed Panamanian notary and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription of the Public Deed in the Mercantile Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección del Registro Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Escritura Pública together with the application for registration and payment of the official inscription fee. The Registry reviews the deed for compliance with Ley 32 de 1927, assigns the corporate Ficha, and records the legal existence of the Sociedad Anónima. The date of inscription determines incorporation date.
required_dossiers: Original notarized Escritura Pública
Name-reservation certificate
Proof of payment of inscription fees
Notary's legalization and compliance certificate
Power of attorney if filed by a legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry files a defect notice (reforma), submit a corrected deed or explanatory response within the granted term; if the term lapses, request ratification or re-inscription through the registered agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Registered Agent and Statutory Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Panama-licensed registered agent under the Public Registry regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Panama-licensed registered agent and confirm the registered office in Panama for service of process. Maintain the corporate minute book, share ledger, register of directors and officers, and a copy of the recorded deed. Prepare the officers' election forms and written consents in Spanish or English.
required_dossiers: Evidence of the licensed registered agent's acceptance
List of initial directors and officers and share allocations
Registered office address confirmation in Panama
Consent forms signed by officers and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered agent declines or the registered office is invalid, appoint a substitute licensed agent and file the change at the Public Registry under the appropriate mercantile filing procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Obtaining the RUC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas – Sistema TAX online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the Registro Único de Contribuyente in the DGI's Sistema TAX platform after the Public Registry records the company. Upload the certified copy of the public deed, corporate registration certificate, identity documents of the legal representative, and prove the registered office address. A tax accountant may submit the application under a tax power of attorney.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Ficha and public deed
Identity document of the legal representative
Tax agent power of attorney, if applicable
Completed DGI registration forms
Proof of office address or lease agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI questions the supporting documents, correct the file in the Sistema TAX portal or attend the DGI service desk, then resubmit the corrected application for processing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operating License – Aviso de Operación
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipio de Panamá – Dirección de Avisos de Operación / Panamá Emprende one-stop window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for the Aviso de Operación or municipal operating permit for the activity 'market research and polling services'. Attach the RUC, corporate registration certificate, lease or property title, and fire-safety certificate. The municipality issues the local operating license before operations begin and requires annual renewal.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate
Certified corporate registration document
Lease agreement or proof of property ownership
Fire-safety inspection certificate issued by the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá
Identity document of the legal representative
Completed municipal application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality requires zoning classification or correct activity code, provide the landlord's authorization or an alternative address, and appeal through the municipal legal directorate if the permit is refused.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Civil Defense Fire Safety and Occupational Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá and Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For any physical office, complete a fire-safety inspection with the Cuerpo de Bomberos, post the inspection certificate, and ensure emergency exits, extinguishers, and electrical load compliance. If the company hires employees, register the workplace with MITRADEL and file occupational health and safety documentation.
required_dossiers: Fire inspection application form
Floor plan and electrical load certificate signed by a licensed engineer
Lease or ownership documents
Corporate registration details
Employee occupational-risk registration forms, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If fire-safety inspection fails, correct the deficiencies, notify the inspector, and request re-inspection within the assigned schedule; for MITRADEL queries, submit the missing employment record or safety policy for clearance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Dirección de Avisos de Operación del Municipio de Panamá, coordinated with the Dirección General de Ingresos and the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; no specialized industrial licensing board applies to a cloud-based consumer polling platform.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación / Permiso Municipal de Operación

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt or Categoría I / Environmental Registration category; a full Environmental Impact Assessment is not required for an office-based market research-and-polling SaaS platform unless it involves physical installations in protected or sensitive areas.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial point-source discharges and no significant VOC or particulate emissions are generated by the platform. Sanitary wastewater from leased offices must comply with applicable Panama health and environmental standards, electronic waste must be handled through certified e-waste recyclers, and any installed generators or air-conditioning equipment must meet refrigerant reuse and emissions rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá annual fire-safety inspection certificate, structural and electrical load certifications by a licensed Panamanian engineer for any leased office, and MITRADEL occupational health-and-safety registration for all employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama. Principal portals: Sede Electrónica at https://sede.dgi.gob.pa (RUC registration, returns and payments); https://www.dgi.gob.pa for official guidance; mandatory electronic invoicing platform SIFED/DGI Patria with API integration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident-owned Panamanian Sociedad Anónima (S.A.): (1) incorporate in the Registro Público under Ley 32 de 1927 and obtain the corporate Ficha Electronica; (2) appoint the statutory resident agent and directors; (3) file the Aviso de Operación with the municipality only if local business activity is carried out in Panama; (4) obtain a digital signature certificate (Firma Electrónica) and, via the DGI Sede Electrónica, submit the Solicitud de Inscripción de Contribuyente together with the Ficha, apostilled Spanish-translated corporate documents, shareholding structure, and intended ISIC 7320 activity to obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes); (5) request electronic invoicing authorisation (habilitación para facturación electrónica) in the same portal; (6) file Form 2410 (Declaración Jurada de Ingresos de Fuente Extranjera) annually and, where Panama-source revenue exists, the Form 2411 corporate income tax return, Form 217 ITBMS returns, and municipal statements. The procedure may be completed remotely through a licensed Panamanian attorney/CPA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Territorial_Scope. The S.A. is a distinct taxable person subject to 25% corporate income tax only on Panama-source income; foreign-source SaaS and market-research income sits outside the Panamanian tax base. Dividends from Panama-source profits incur 10% withholding (20% in certain undistributed/unreported profit scenarios); no pass-through treatment is available; ITBMS zero-rating applies to exported services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama has no US-style check-the-box and no flow-through election for S.A. companies. The territorial regime applies automatically; available elections include: (i) the Régimen de Pequeño Contribuyente for annual turnover up to B/. 36,000 (presumptive ITBMS); (ii) the Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime under Law 41 of 2007, granting preferential taxation on qualifying foreign-source services subject to an approved SEM licence and local substance; (iii) election of monthly vs quarterly ITBMS filing depending on taxable volume (B/. 300,000 threshold); (iv) no hybrid-mismatch election exists, although BEPS-aligned transfer-pricing rules mandate arm's-length documentation for controlled cross-border transactions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no central bank. Monetary and FX framework is organized around the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panama (SBP), which supervises banks and enforces AML/CFT under Law 42 of 2001, and the Banco Nacional de Panama (state-owned), which issues the fractional Balboa coinage alongside the U.S. Dollar as legal tender. The SBP also operates the official payment/clearing infrastructure (ACH Panama and SWIFT environment), while the U.S. Federal Reserve de facto sets monetary conditions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full and unrestricted convertibility in both current and capital accounts. The Balboa (PAB) is fixed at 1:1 to the USD and exists only as coins; USD banknotes circulate freely. There are no exchange controls, no central bank authorization for outward remittances, no limits on dividend/profit repatriation, and no restrictions on non-resident ownership of Panamanian S.A. shares or capital accounts. A foreign-owned S.A. may hold, receive, and disburse USD indefinitely inside or outside Panama without approval. The only practical hurdles are (i) proving to the DGI that income is territorial (non-Panamanian source) when repatriating, and (ii) satisfying bank source-of-funds and beneficial-ownership KYC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Panama imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender obligation on export or cross-border service receipts. Proceeds from consumer polling / market research SaaS services (ISIC 7320 / NAICS 541910) may be retained in USD in Panamanian or offshore accounts without central bank filing. For bank compliance, such proceeds are recorded as service-export income and must be supported by executed client master service agreements, itemized invoices, and audience-panel delivery reports; no Balboa conversion or repatriation deadline applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (USD multibusiness, collections and disbursements)
Operational Account (USD, with regional LatAm treasury desk)
Capital Escrow Account and Operational USD Account
Reserved for local payroll/public-sector operations; not recommended for non-resident S.A.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a bank substitute, Medium as a payment utility. Panama does not operate a full e-money institution license regime; Panama's banking law (Decree-Law 9 of 1998) requires any institution collecting funds from the public to be licensed by the SBP. Offshore EMIs (e.g., UK FCA or EU-licensed entities) cannot lawfully hold client money for a Panamanian S.A. as a domestic bank replacement. The SBP innovation sandbox (Law 76 of 2021) permits supervised fintech pilots but does not yet grant full EMIs to third-country firms. Practical approach: use Wise and PayPal Mass Payout as registered remittance/PSP channels that settle into a domestic SBP-licensed bank account, while treasury cash balances remain with a Tier-1 Panamanian commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Effectively mandated for first onboarding. Tier-1 Panamanian banks require in-person KYC interviews at a Panamanian branch for the beneficial owner and the legal representative / authorized signatories before account activation; a local resident agent alone is not sufficient. Remote account opening is occasionally accepted (e.g., Global Bank, Towerbank) only with (i) apostilled notarial corporate documents, (ii) apostilled board resolutions granting power of attorney, (iii) video-verified identity, and (iv) an existing private banking/correspondent referral, but this is discretionary and slower. Plan for one physical visit of the UBO to Panama City; post-onboarding remote treasury management is standard.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undisclosed beneficial ownership or historical bearer-share structure in the Panamanian S.A.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current notarial share ledger and share certificates; certification from the resident agent (abogado) that no bearer shares exist and that beneficial ownership records are maintained under Law 23 of 2015; excerpt of the DGI Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (RBF) showing the ultimate individual; full corporate bylaws and registry certificate from the Registro Publico.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital panel survey income arriving from PayPal/Wise in fragmented low-value transfers from many countries, flagged as unexplained float.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12-month PayPal and Wise payout statements; executed client contracts (sample/brand tracker agreements); platform invoice batch logs; panelist payment history with survey ID references; management accounts showing the conversion of survey receipts into net revenue; written AML policy of the platform covering panelist onboarding and payment distribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Allegation of insufficient economic substance in Panama (shell-risk under SBP enhanced KYC).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Rent or service-desk agreement in Panama City; payroll or outsourced corporate administration agreement; resident agent certification; Aviso de Operacion (business notice) filed at the Registro Publico; business plan of the ISIC 7320 platform; minutes of at least two board meetings held during the account review period; local accountant engagement letter for statutory books.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions / PEP / restricted-jurisdiction exposure within the consumer panel respondent base.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated OFAC, EU, UN and PEP screening output for the respondent database; contractual prohibition on payments to sanctioned persons in the panelist terms of use; IP/geo-blocking policy; documented country risk matrix for respondent jurisdictions; internal procedure for freezing and reporting suspicious survey payouts to the Unidad de Analisis Financiero (UAF).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injection is executed by SWIFT MT103 (or FedWire via the U.S. correspondent of the beneficiary bank) from the shareholder's account to the S.A.'s USD operational account. Field 50K must identify the shareholder; Field 59 the S.A. beneficiary account; Field 70 remittance information must read 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION / EQUITY INJECTION PER BOARD RESOLUTION NO. [X] DATED [YYYY-MM-DD]'. The bank requires the notarized shareholders'/board resolution authorizing the injection, updated share register evidencing issuance, and, for amounts above USD 500,000, a sworn source-of-funds affidavit. No DGI or SBP prior approval is required for capital-account inflows; the treasury file must retain the SWIFT confirmation, bank credit advice, and resolution for later DGI territorial-income defense and CRS/FATCA reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Three-tier clearing structure: (1) Panelist incentives/rewards below USD 1,000 per payment are batched via PayPal Mass Payout API and Wise batch transfers, each instruction carrying a memo of 'Panel reward - survey [ID]', funded from the S.A. USD account; (2) B2B vendor invoices (sampling agencies, translators, data hosts) are settled by SWIFT MT103 using SWIFT gpi with remittance referencing the contract and invoice number and narrative 'Commercial services - market research (ISIC 7320)'; (3) For procurement of physical goods (survey hardware, ad-sample materials) exceeding USD 10,000, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit (sight or 30-90 days usance) is issued through the Tier-1 bank's trade desk. All outbound payments are recorded against a purpose-code memo internally matching Panamanian territorial-income rules so that foreign-source costs are properly documented and no Panama-source income leakage occurs.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot outright FX transactions (USD vs EUR, GBP, JPY, MXN, COP, ARS) with SBP-licensed banks
Plain-vanilla outright forwards (delivery or cash-settled) on EUR/USD, GBP/USD executed under ISDA or bank master agreement with the Tier-1 Panamanian bank
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on Latin American restricted-currency pairs (ARS, COP, BRL, MXN, PEN) where the USD leg is settled in Panama
Cross-currency swaps (XCCY) for medium-term USD/EUR positions, subject to bank treasury credit approval and ISDA collateral annex
European-style FX options (call/put on USD crosses) offered by the bank's treasury desk for hedging panel-payout currency exposure
FX limit orders and algorithmic hedging via the bank's online treasury portal for recurring small-ticket panel payouts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax Payment (Impuesto Anual de Sociedades Anónimas)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) - Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% surcharge (US$30) for payments made April 1 through June 30; monthly interest accrual after June 30; administrative strike-off of the entity after two consecutive years of non-payment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Confirmation/Update (Registro de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership; annual confirmation required at the time of the March 31 franchise tax payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines and restrictions on registration of corporate acts for failure to file or update the beneficial owner declaration; DGI monetary penalties may apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de Impuesto sobre la Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI - Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 of the year following the close of the fiscal year (or within three months of a different fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% per month of tax due, up to a maximum of 50%; monthly interest on unpaid tax; administrative assessment and potential judicial enforcement for persistent non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Tax-resident corporations with Panamanian-source gross income exceeding B/.500,000 or total year-end assets exceeding B/.1,000,000 must file audited financial statements with the annual income tax return. Entities listed on a securities exchange are subject to separate mandatory audit obligations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as issued by the IASB; IFRS for SMEs is permitted for entities without public accountability and with annual revenue below B/.3,000,000.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: After any share transfer, a written transfer instrument must be executed and recorded in the Register of Members; the resident agent must update the beneficial ownership record and, under Law 129 (2020), notify the DGI Beneficial Owner Registry within 30 business days. An annual written confirmation from directors is recommended at the time of the March 31 franchise tax payment, expressly stating there are no undisclosed shareholding changes during the tax year.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial-source taxation: foreign-source fee income of the cross-border survey platform (ISIC 7320 SaaS) invoiced to non-resident clients and delivered outside Panama is excluded from the Panamanian tax base, producing an effective 0% Panama tax burden on that revenue. No broad statutory tax holiday is available to a plain S.A.; however, Law 254 of 2024 applies a reduced 20% rate to the first USD 1.5 million of Panama-source taxable income, with the 25% headline rate on the excess. Selective regimes (SEM Multinational Headquarters Law 41/2007, free-zone and Ciudad del Saber incentives) exist but require qualifying physical substance and are not presumed for a shell S.A.
